text.p: Homeowners Group Inc said Friday it may face a $7 million tax bill, upsetting its merger plans with privately held Cross Country Group.
Homeowners said it received Internal Revenue Service (IRS) notices, holding the company liable for about $7 million of tax, plus interest and possible penalties.

As a result, the Cross Country Group notified the company it would not go ahead with the proposed merger at this time, Homeowners said. Homeowners added it is still discussing modifications to the merger agreement, which expires July 1. Homeowners said it "intends to vigorously contest the IRS position." The IRS sent Homeowners notices of proposed adjustment for the tax years 1993, 1994 and 1994, which would disallow losses totaling about $20.5 million, the company said.
Homeowners said it postponed its shareholders meeting scheduled for June 19. NASDAQ trading in Homeowners shares was halted.
